name: memphis-data-centers
note: Data centres in Memphis, with a one-mile and five-mile profile of the ground around each. Rings are drawn on the map; the profile counts what is inside them. Population and demographics come from whole census tracts, so they are reported as the tracts mostly inside the ring where there are any, and otherwise as every tract the ring touches, which is stated on the page. A one-mile ring is smaller than a census tract, so 'people within a mile' is not a number the census can answer. Operator is who runs the compute today; owner is who built and holds the site. They are not the same at Colossus 1, and the distinction is the whole point of naming either.

sources.sites: Memphis Chamber announcement June 2024 and site addresses; coordinates geocoded from the addresses
sources.acs: Shelby Co Tract ACS Demo 5Y 2024, data.memphistn.gov
sources.assets: City of Memphis parks, libraries, community centers; USDA SNAP retailers
sources.flood: FEMA flood zones as carried in data/flood.geojson

properties.name: Colossus 1
properties.street: 3231 Paul R Lowry Rd, Memphis, TN 38109
properties.note: Built by xAI in the former Electrolux plant near Boxtown. xAI has moved its own operations to Colossus 2, and as of 6 May 2026 Anthropic rents all of the compute capacity here, reported at more than 300MW and about $1.25 billion a month through May 2029. The turbines, the water draw and the neighbours are the same ones; the tenant changed.

declared.power: 150MW grid connection at the 2024 announcement, reported over 300MW of capacity in 2026
declared.water: 1 to 1.5 million gallons a day at the 2024 announcement; over 5 million a day reported at full capacity

properties.name: Colossus 2
properties.status: Operating · xAI moved here from Colossus 1
properties.note: The Whitehaven site, bought through an xAI affiliate in March 2025. xAI moved its own operations here when Colossus 1 went to Anthropic, so this is the site xAI now runs.
